title: Shah Rukh Khan Opens America’s First Franchise-Built Cricket Stadium in Los Angeles
excerpt: The $21 million Knight Riders Cricket Ground hosted its inaugural MLC match and will serve as a venue for cricket’s return to the Olympics in 2028
body:
When Shah Rukh Khan posted a video on X calling the Knight Riders Cricket Ground “a dream that turns into reality,” he was not exaggerating. On July 1, the Bollywood superstar and his Knight Riders Group officially inaugurated a dedicated cricket stadium at the Fairplex in Pomona, California — making them the first cricket franchise in history to build and own an international-standard venue.

The ground hosted its first-ever Major League Cricket match the same day, with the Los Angeles Knight Riders squaring off against Washington Freedom in the opening fixture of the 2026 MLC season. Washington won the low-scoring contest by six wickets, but the real story was the venue itself — a 10-acre, purpose-built facility constructed at a cost of roughly $21 million (₹199 crore).

## A Stadium Built for the Olympics

The Knight Riders Cricket Ground features eight wickets on the main square, ICC-standard playing dimensions, and six floodlight towers standing 120 feet tall. More than 32,000 metric tonnes of earth were moved during construction to shape the arena.

Currently seating around 5,000 spectators, the venue will expand to 12,000 by 2027 and 15,000 by 2028 — when it is set to host cricket matches during the Los Angeles Olympic Games. That will mark cricket’s return to the Olympics for the first time since the 1900 Paris Games, a gap of 128 years.

“Bringing cricket, the second most-watched sport in the world, to Los Angeles is a landmark moment for all of us,” Khan said. “Through this long-term partnership between Fairplex and Knight Riders, we are creating much more than a cricket venue. We are building a space that celebrates community, togetherness, energy and entertainment.”

> **"“Bringing cricket, the second most-watched sport in the world, to Los Angeles is a landmark moment for all of us,” Khan said."**

## The Match That Christened It

The debut fixture provided plenty of drama. Los Angeles Knight Riders captain Jason Holder won the toss and chose to bat — a decision that backfired as his side collapsed from 46 for one to 108 all out in 17.5 overs.

Indian-American pace bowler **Saurabh Netravalkar** was the star of the match, claiming three economical wickets for Washington Freedom alongside Australian all-rounder Mitchell Owen. Netravalkar, who grew up in Mumbai before moving to the United States and now works as a software engineer at Oracle when he is not playing cricket, has become one of the most recognizable faces of American cricket.

![Los Angeles — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5a/Hollywood_Sign_%28Zuschnitt%29.jpg/3840px-Hollywood_Sign_%28Zuschnitt%29.jpg)

Washington Freedom’s Steve Smith anchored the chase with an unbeaten 40 off 44 balls, and Freedom cruised to victory with 17 balls to spare.

## Cricket’s American Moment

Adding a distinctly cross-sport flavour to the occasion, NBA champion Ron Artest — better known as Metta World Peace — bowled the ceremonial first ball.

The Knight Riders Cricket Ground will host MLC matches through July 5 before the tournament moves to other venues, culminating in the playoffs at Oakland Coliseum from July 15 to 18. The MLC’s fourth season runs from June 18 to July 18, featuring six franchises across venues in Texas and California.

Knight Riders Sports CEO Venky Mysore called the stadium “a statement of intent for the future of cricket,” adding: “Becoming the first global cricket brand to establish an international cricket stadium is a proud milestone for the Knight Riders Group.”

## What It Means for Desi Fans in America

For the estimated 4.8 million Indian Americans — many of whom grew up watching cricket but have had few opportunities to experience it live in the US — the Knight Riders Cricket Ground represents something larger than a sports venue.

The stadium arrives at a pivotal moment for American cricket. The 2028 LA Olympics will bring unprecedented global attention to the sport on American soil, and MLC is positioning itself as the domestic league to capture that wave. With Bollywood’s biggest star as the face of the franchise and a world-class venue in the second-largest American metro area, the Knight Riders are betting that the Indian diaspora’s appetite for live cricket will anchor the sport’s growth in the country.

Khan himself put it simply: “This is for LA, for cricket fans across the globe, and for the Knight Riders family.”
